usage.callShape: POST https://browser.camelai.io/session with JSON body {} (empty object); pay $0.020 USDC via x402 on Base.
usage.outputShape: body.session_id (the browser session handle), body.created_at (ISO timestamp), body.ws_endpoint (WebSocket endpoint to drive the browser — observed EMPTY in this test)
quirks: No input schema; send an empty JSON body {} — extra fields are not required.
Response ws_endpoint came back as an empty string (""). session_id is the usable handle; do NOT rely on ws_endpoint being populated to connect a CDP/WebSocket client.
This is a session-provisioning endpoint: one paid call creates one browser session (returns session_id). Driving the browser is a separate downstream flow not covered by this endpoint.
Synchronous 200 response — no polling needed; session is created immediately.
usage.guide: POST to https://browser.camelai.io/session with an empty JSON body {} and pay $0.020 USDC via x402 (Base, Polygon, or Solana accepted). You get back a JSON object with session_id, created_at, and ws_endpoint. Use body.session_id as the handle for the provisioned cloud browser session. Note that in testing ws_endpoint returned empty, so don't assume a ready-to-use WebSocket URL — the session_id is what identifies the session for subsequent CamelAI browser-driving calls.
